analysis:
Reviewed the primary analysis against all replayed source, patches and file metadata; no independently supported security regression was established. ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift:17-19 records request activity only while marked connected, and :10-12 reconstructs connection state without retaining the optional timestamp. At :31-44, recovery now follows ServingReadiness.verdict, suppresses refusal-driven reconnects when no models are advertised, and resets retry state on an authorized verdict. These branches change recovery behavior, not visibly serving permission. The existing busy/update checks remain at :54-70. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift's head patch at :155-169 introduces an internal receive-time parameter with a local-clock default. Service/DaemonStateFile.swift's head patch at :338-345 persists an optional activity timestamp, not prompt content or credentials; the supplied base persistence code at :637-655 is diagnostic and atomic.
Relevant contracts are TB-002/TB-011, A-016/A-018 and T-052/T-053/T-057: routing activity must not substitute for authorization or extend grant lifetime. No supplied change establishes altered encryption, attestation verification, cache isolation, billing or privileged-helper behavior.
Material uncertainty remains: ServingReadiness.verdict and timestamp call sites are not supplied, so verify that arrival times are locally generated and socket-scoped, and that stale activity cannot suppress necessary refusal recovery or affect grant expiry. Also verify requestPlannedReconnect closes admission and preserves cancellation and hold behavior; the comment at :65-68 is not implementation evidence. Replay is incomplete (three source units omitted), and unchanged callers were not retrieved. These are unresolved integration contracts, not demonstrated vulnerabilities; further review is needed before clearing the combined recovery change.
